StockSenseInventory & Warehouse Management

A database-backed workspace for products, locations, receipts, deliveries, transfers, and stock adjustments — connected by an auditable movement ledger.

  • Next.js
  • TypeScript
  • PostgreSQL

ONE LEDGER. FOUR OPERATIONS.

↙ReceiptIncoming → increase stock
↗DeliveryCheck availability → outgoing
⇄TransferLocation A → location B
±AdjustmentPhysical count → reconciliation
NEXT.JS → BUSINESS RULESPRISMA → POSTGRESQL

The problem

Inventory operations need a consistent record of what moved, where it moved, and why. Products, locations, and operational changes must remain connected.

Who it is for

Inventory managers and warehouse staff managing the stock lifecycle across locations.

Engineering challenge

Enforce business invariants on the server: reject invalid location hierarchies, check stock availability on delivery, and preserve total stock during internal transfers.

Architecture

  1. Next.js interface → REST-style API routes
  2. Server-side business rules → Prisma ORM
  3. PostgreSQL → products + locations + stock movements
  4. Authenticated workspace → signed HTTP-only sessions

Simplified architecture based on repository documentation.

Technology choices

  • Next.js
  • TypeScript
  • PostgreSQL
  • Prisma

The stack above is documented in the repository. The architecture separates interface, execution or business logic, and persistence.

Documented implementation

  • SKU-based product management and search
  • Warehouse-aware locations with hierarchy validation
  • Receipts, deliveries, internal transfers, and adjustments
  • Movement history, low-stock indicators, and OTP authentication

Current limits

Repository documentation describes the implementation. A public deployment, customer usage, and production acceptance have not been independently verified.

Design takeaway

Business software earns clarity through explicit data relationships and server-side rules, with the ledger preserving an inspectable history.

This is an architectural interpretation of the documented implementation, not a measured outcome or a personal claim.
